description: The four voices of the Nintendo Game Boy sound chip: two pulses, a drawable wavetable and a noise generator

params.text: Sets the pitch of that voice, two and a half octaves either side of C4
Sets the pitch of the noise, 0 to 7, with the highest setting giving the shortest period and so the brightest hiss
Attenuates the voltage at that voice's MOD jack before it is added to the pitch, and inverts it below zero
Picks the noise flavour: one position gives the long fifteen-bit sequence, which sounds like hiss, the other the short seven-bit sequence, which sounds metallic and pitched
Picks the duty cycle of that pulse, 0 to 3, giving an eighth, a quarter, a half or three quarters
Morphs between the five drawn waveforms, 1 to 5, interpolating sample by sample between neighbouring pairs
Sets the level of that voice, 0 to 15
Sets the level of the wavetable voice in four steps: silent, a quarter, a half and full

inputs.text: Raises the pitch of that voice by a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the VOCT jack of the voice before it, and the first pulse reads 0V
Moves the noise pitch, each 2V raising it by one step, and does nothing until a cable is patched
Modulates the pitch of that voice, a full octave per 5V with the MOD knob wide open; unpatched it reads the MOD jack of the voice before it, and the first pulse reads 5V
Flips the noise flavour set by the LFSR switch while it is above 2V
Moves the duty cycle of that pulse through 0 to 7V; unpatched it reads the PW jack of the first pulse, which itself reads 0V
Moves the waveform morph, 7V spanning all five waveforms; unpatched it reads the second pulse's PW jack
Scales that voice's AMP knob by the voltage here, 10V leaving the knob untouched and 0V silencing it; unpatched it reads the AMP jack of the voice before it, and the first pulse reads 10V

outputs.text: Carries that voice's audio, hard clipped at 5V, with the audio of any earlier voice whose own output is unpatched added in

notes: the five waveform displays are drawn on with the mouse: drag across one to reshape it. The WAVE knob morphs between them in the order red, green, blue, yellow, white
the four outputs are chained: a voice whose output is left unpatched is summed into the next output along, so patching only NOISE gives a mix of all four
